To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The Academic Senate has a latent organizational function in the university that is to provide faculty members with an identity, a voice, and a place to go for help.

(a) senates have three latent functions: (i) they provide faculty with the means to express their opinions, (ii) they provide faculty and the administration with a forum for the exchange of information, and (iii) they provide faculty members with an identity; (b) the three functions are interrelated; (c) the functions are not necessarily conscious to the participants; (d) the functions are independent of the structure of the senate, and (e) the functions are relatively stable
(a) the academic senate is not an organization, and (b) the academic senate performs latent organizational functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the latent organizational functions of the senate as a governance structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
senates are the normative structure of faculty governance at the institutional (or college) level.
senates are not effective, but that the reasons they are not effective are not necessarily the same as those that would lead to their disappearance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the senate is a necessary but insufficient condition for effective faculty governance at the institutional or campus level.
senates, although they may not be the most effective means of achieving faculty participation in institutional governance, have become the most common and are likely to be the most durable.
the senate is a necessary but not sufficient component of faculty participation in governance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Senate is a latent function of the institution.
the organizational form and function of the academic senate are not well understood and that there is a need for more research on senates.

, in the absence of a more robust understanding of how faculty members view their roles and responsibilities as members of the academic senate, it will be difficult for the senate to be a more effective vehicle for the advancement of faculty concerns.
